_comment: Phase D regime (c): selective-refusal missingness (study plan 8.5(c), 6.4).
PROVISIONAL -- nothing here is frozen until E3.
Refusals are NOT missing at random: a model that declines to choose does so
disproportionately on menus where the alternatives are close, which are
exactly the menus carrying the most information about alpha. Dropping them
leaves an easier-looking choice set, so alpha should be biased UPWARD.
Every rate is fitted TWICE per iteration: targeted at low eta-gap menus, and
missing-at-random at the same rate as the control. The MAR arm drops the
same COUNT, so any difference between the arms is the cost of TARGETING
rather than of lost sample size. With the complete-data fit that is 3 fits
Starting at the STRESS rate 0.25 alone. If a quarter of choices going
missing selectively produces no material alpha bias, no smaller rate will
either. Add 0.10 for a dose-response only if 0.25 shows something.
rho_copy 0.9 and menus/cell 30 match the regime (a) reference cell so the
timing basis and the pseudo-replication regime are comparable.
